newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa turns up in afternoon with NY, ends up.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa turns up in afternoon with NY, ends up.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed stonger after New York's sharp rise at the open pulled in some trade and speculative buying here to push prices higher in the afternoon.

May ended up four stg at 1,021 stg per tonne and July gained seven to 1,039. Both contracts reached their highest levels since April 7, the day heavy fund sales in New York sparked a sell-off that dragged prices down more than five percent.

Trade buying in New York triggered buy-stops, which pushed CSCE July cocoa up to a 1-1/2 week high. But July met stiff resistance at a chart gap between the April 7 high of $1,480 and the previous session's low of $1,501.
New York's failure to fill the gap stymied gains for now. But traders still expected another test higher unless scale-up origin selling in London becomes more aggressive and holds back gains.
They said speculative sales linked to May's first notice day in New York were no longer hanging over the market, and prices now had room to rise.
Once July closes in on its April 2 peak of 1,065, they expected fund buying to emerge and further lift prices to new highs.
July support was seen at 980, the April 9 low.
December continued to trade at a discount to July and September, indicating that the market was still pricing in a cocoa shortage.

Though the spread between December and July has stabilized with July near a 16-stg premium to December, December's spread against September has widened. September commanded a 24-stg premium to December, up from about 17 at midmorning on Wednesday.

At 1345 GMT on Friday, U.S. first-quarter grind data are due. U.S. analysts and traders' forecasts ranged from flat to up five percent. But traders generally did not expect much reaction to the figures.

Total volume tallied 7,592 contracts, with more than two-thirds coming in the afternoon session. July took the biggest chunk with 2,996 contracts changing hands. May followed with 2,208 lots. All other contracts tallied fewer than 1,000 contracts.
In options, 10 July 1,200 stg calls traded in the afternoon.
